setup.description:
Fixture built by shelling out to the real `git` CLI`), not git2 — this is deliberate in the original test, so the stash messages carry git's own 'On <branch>: ' prefix convention exactly as a real `git stash push -m` would produce them. Sequence: `git init -q`; `git config user.email/user.name`; write a.txt = 'one
', `git add .`, `git commit -q -m init`. Then: write a.txt = 'two
', `git stash push -q -m "first stash"`. Then: write a.txt = 'three
', `git stash push -q -m "second stash"`. Resulting stash stack (index 0 = newest): stash@{0} message contains 'second stash', stash@{1} message contains 'first stash' — both prefixed by git with 'On <branch>: ', so the original test asserts containment, not equality, to stay independent of the host's default branch name.

steps: call list_stashes(repo_path) — assert length 2, [0].message contains "second stash", [1].message contains "first stash"
cases.notes: Renaming index 0 (already the newest) does not reorder anything. Unlike the original git-CLI-created messages, the reappended message is the caller's new_message used verbatim — no 'On <branch>: ' prefix is added by rename_stash's own repo.reference(...) call, so stash_0_message_after is an exact match, not a containment check.

setup.description: Same fixture as rename-top-stash-keeps-order — two stashes, stash@{0}='second stash', stash@{1}='first stash' (both git-CLI-prefixed with 'On <branch>: ').

cases.notes: Renaming index 1 (the older, non-top stash) drops it via stash_drop(1) and reappends it as the new refs/stash HEAD, so it becomes stash@{0} and the stash that used to be stash@{0} ('second stash') shifts down to stash@{1} unmodified. No stash is lost or duplicated: length stays 2. This is the documented reordering side effect of rename_stash (GIT-014 / DIVERGENCE-GIT-a) — the same trade-off as `git stash pop && git stash push -m "..."`.
